title: Pay finite cooldown and retain the logical damage already emitted
statement: With forces OFF, chi ON, fixed Z1 as an operator, no further noncommuting faults/controls and cold Markov outlets, the g=1, Gamma=4, chi=2 model with 0<=kb,kc<=1e-4 obeys ||E_plus/minus(t)||^2<=.145^floor(gt/4). The supplied proof uses exact integer Taylor/minor certificates and contractive Duhamel bounds, including the nonnormal transient. For arbitrary apparatus states entangled with data/reference and mean occupation <=Emax, p_nonvac<=Emax*.145^floor(gt/4). Half trace distance to the ACTUAL POST-COOLING data/reference marginal tensored with vacuum is <=sqrt(p)+p/2, retaining any logical damage emitted while cooling. Enforced drive action 30 and T=8 give Emax=240 for the stated Pauli-fault trajectories. Cooldowns 40/g for distance .001 and 72/g for 1e-6 are sufficient, not minimum times. Without an acquired fault/energy flag, every reuse pays the wait; a parity outcome is not that flag. Turning chi off leaves a dark mode. Unbounded injection, arbitrary sign switching and extra noncommuting faults are outside the proof. The warm reference floor is about .002994 at n_in=.001; the nonzero cold auxiliary-loss covariance has a separate numerical result .00299361164. Idle faults, routing and isolation remain costs.
